updates.missing: The ecommerce shelf has no capability for abandoned-cart recovery (seeing abandoned carts, reminding the shopper, tracking carts won back) — only a one-line intelligence feature. Proposed: a new capability 'Abandoned-cart recovery' under ecommerce. No web research was possible in this run; drafted from the shelves and the owner's statement.
updates.draft:
- **Abandoned-cart recovery** — win back the sales a shopper started and left.
  A cart that holds items but ends with no order is a lost sale the operator can
  still recover; the capability makes those carts visible to the operator and
  brings the shopper back to finish. It serves the shopper's *Acquire* intent
  ("let me buy it") when it broke off, and the operator's *Understand* intent.
  Sending the message is `notifications` (channel delivery, consent, frequency);
  measuring the win-back is `analytics` (conversion funnel); this capability owns
  the decision of WHICH cart, WHEN, and the way back into the same cart.
  - Abandoned-cart detection — mark a cart abandoned when it holds items and no order follows within a set window. The floor — every store that sells.
  - Operator view of abandoned carts — list the carts abandoned in a period (e.g. today) with shopper, items and value, so the operator knows which sales could still be won back. The floor wherever an operator runs the store.
  - Cart reminder — operator-triggered (one click) or automatic message to the shopper that their cart is waiting, with a link that restores the same cart. Add when the shopper can be reached away from the store (`notifications` → Channel delivery); requires opt-in where `nfr.privacy >= medium` or `compliance` includes GDPR.
  - Recovery tracking — count reminded carts that end in an order and the sales won back, over time. Add when the business sets a win-back goal (`analytics` → Goals, Funnels).
  - Reminder sequences & incentives — timed follow-ups and an optional offer (next-best-offer / personalised promotion). Add when `shape.stage` is public/monetized and fatigue control is in place.
  - Abandonment prediction & in-session nudge — spot a cart likely to be abandoned and nudge while the shopper is still present (`experience` governed nudges). Add when real-time presence signals are reliable (the shelf's core *Acquire* intelligence line).

updates.missing: How long a cart must sit with items and no order (and no activity) before it counts as abandoned — the default abandonment window for Seeing today's abandoned carts. Memory says only "within a set window" (short-term 1/context/answers/kb/ecommerce-abandoned-cart-recovery.md line 9) and names no length.
updates.draft: A cart counts as abandoned when it holds at least one item, no order has been placed from it, and nobody has touched it for 60 minutes. The 60 minutes is one shop-wide default for the MVP; owners cannot change it yet.

updates.missing: How many days after a cart is abandoned an order from that cart still counts as the cart won back (the win-back window used to count carts won back and to close each month). No memory tier holds a value; the abandoned-cart recovery answer only says a set window exists.
updates.draft: The win-back window is one platform-wide setting, in days after a cart is marked abandoned. Proposed starting value: 7 days, to be confirmed or replaced by the head of the shop-owner side. The same window applies to every month and to each shop's baseline month, and a change to it recomputes baselines with the change dated.

updates.missing: Which privacy or data-protection regimes (for example GDPR) apply to the shoppers whose carts and orders the platform counts. No memory tier and no source statement names the regions the shops sell in, so carts-won-back records no compliance need until a person answers.
updates.draft: Unknown until a person answers: no source names the regions the shops sell to. Until then no regime is assumed; the carts-won-back capability already keeps shopper personal details out of every figure and matches on cart id only, which holds under GDPR as well.

updates.missing: Which consent regimes apply to the abandoned-cart reminder email. It depends on where the shops' customers live; no memory tier says which regions this product serves. The marketing shelf names GDPR / CAN-SPAM as the regimes that govern consent for reach.
updates.draft: The abandoned-cart reminder is an email to a customer who has left the shop, so it is treated as reach that needs consent. Regimes to list in compliance_needs depend on where customers live: GDPR (and the matching e-privacy rules) if any customers are in the EU or UK; CAN-SPAM if any are in the US. Until a person confirms the regions, no regime is listed, and the capability still enforces opt-in before sending and a one-click opt-out in every reminder, because the product privacy level is medium or higher.

updates.missing: How often the same customer may be reminded across different abandoned carts. Memory says cap low-value sends and never spam, but gives no number.
updates.draft: A customer receives at most one abandoned-cart reminder per cart, ever, and at most one reminder from the same shop in any 7-day window, even across different carts. Timed follow-up sequences are not used at this stage (MVP).

updates.missing: How long the abandoned-cart Reminder record keeps its entries (retention length)
updates.draft: No retention length is set in any memory tier, and none is proposed here. The product owner sets it. Constraint from the model: it must cover every month the win-back views show and recompute (from each shop baseline month onward), so no Reminder record entry is deleted until the length is decided.
